locator.title: Наливной пол трескается и пылит? В чем может быть ошибка
locator.lead: Разбираем ошибки при заливке наливного пола, которые часто приводят к проблемам

nearest_text_before.text: Проблема: пропуск этапа работы с инструментом после заливки. Последствие — образование бугров, ям и кратеров на поверхности.

image_reading: A close, oblique macro view shows a gray floor surface with many small pits, pinholes, and several larger crater-like depressions.
The surface is the only semantic entity; no worker, tool, liquid flow, or unambiguous action direction is visible.
Shallow focus and the receding surface provide limited but readable depth, while the defects and rigid surface geometry must remain unchanged.
analysis.article_context: The body image illustrates the visible consequence of skipping spreading and deaeration after pouring: an uneven self-leveling floor marked by pits and crater-like defects, setting up the following corrective steps.

structured_intent.editorial_meaning: Emphasize the cratered, uneven result associated with neglected spreading and deaeration of a poured floor.
structured_intent.initial_state: A static close-up of a gray rigid floor surface covered with small pits and crater-like depressions, seen obliquely with shallow depth of field.
structured_intent.primary_action: The camera performs one bounded lateral track across the existing pitted surface.
structured_intent.terminal_state: The final frame shows a slightly shifted view with a little more of the already visible neighboring pitted surface revealed while the main defect cluster remains recognizable.
structured_intent.geometry_invariant: The floor remains one rigid continuous plane, with every pit and crater fixed to the surface and retaining its shape.
structured_intent.identity_invariant: One floor surface and the existing defect field remain; no tools, people, material, or new pits appear or disappear.
structured_intent.semantic_invariant: The visible surface remains a damaged, inadequately deaerated floor through the final frame.
structured_intent.feasibility_assessment: The image clearly proves a rigid pitted surface and limited depth from oblique perspective and focus falloff, but it shows no tool, hand, liquid motion, contact point, or defensible process direction. Subject animation would invent mechanics; a bounded source-grounded camera move is feasible.

models.scene_plan: Over five seconds, begin an immediate, smooth lateral camera track parallel to the surface, focused on the central cluster of craters. Maintain a moderate constant pace, producing a clearly readable foreground displacement of roughly 7% of frame width without leaving the source-supported surface. Ease gently near the end as a little more of the already visible adjacent pitted area enters the composition; the surface and every defect remain rigid and unchanged.
models.positive_prompt: The camera tracks steadily sideways across the rigid pitted floor, keeping the central crater cluster in focus as nearby foreground pits shift about 7% of the frame through natural parallax. The defects retain their exact shapes and count, ending with a slightly broader adjacent patch of the same damaged surface visible.

models.scene_plan: Use the full five seconds for one even lateral glide across the shallow surface depth, keeping the main crater cluster as the focal target. Start promptly, continue at a calm uniform speed, and decelerate only near the final frames. Limit screen-space travel to about 8% of frame width so provider expansion cannot overextend the move; finish on a modestly shifted view of the same existing defect field without altering or generating pits.
models.positive_prompt: The camera glides laterally across the pitted floor while the central defects stay recognizable and foreground pits move no more than about 8% of the frame through parallax. It settles with a slightly wider neighboring area of the same damaged surface visible, with every crater fixed in shape and position on the floor.

models.scene_plan: For the four-second shot, start a concise lateral camera move immediately and maintain an even speed toward the central crater cluster, with a gentle slowdown only at the end. Target approximately 6% foreground displacement—enough to read at normal speed while preserving the tight macro framing. End with a small additional portion of the existing adjacent surface visible; no defect changes shape, count, or location.
models.positive_prompt: The camera moves sideways at a steady real-time pace across the rigid pitted floor, holding focus on the central crater cluster as foreground pits shift about 6% of the frame by natural parallax. By the final frame, a little more of the already visible neighboring defect field is shown, and all pits remain fixed and unchanged.
